terra.problem: The passage does not say the man previously had sight and speech, so saying he got them back adds a detail.
The waiting-room joke places a modern detail into the man's Bible story rather than using it as a comparison.
Calling the man's trip the shortest commute adds a detail about his journey that the passage does not give.
Saying the man got his sight and speech back assumes he had them before. The passage does not say that.
The cited verse identifies Elijah as the Tishbite but does not call him a prophet. A reference such as 1 Kings 18:36 supports that identification.
The passage calls them the Pharisees' sons but does not say how well the Pharisees know them.
Jesus says the Pharisees' sons will be their judges, but the explanation specifies what they will judge beyond what He says.
Saying Jesus has no spot for standing behind Him turns the answer word into a claim the passage does not make.
Saying Jesus' line is said with care assigns a manner to His words that the text does not give.
The line about a quiet house having a full heart is confusing rather than illuminating or funny.
The smaller-mustache joke has no clear connection to whispering, so its logic does not click.
The explanation equates careless words with words spoken without a plan. Unplanned words are not necessarily careless.
